ukmt-pink-2017-02.title: Think of the centre path
ukmt-pink-2017-02.body:
The centre of the wheel stays one radius from the curve. On the straight slopes it moves parallel to them; at each peak it goes round a circular arc; at each trough it changes direction sharply, with no arc. This is diagram E.

**Answer: (E)**

ukmt-pink-2017-03.title: Count between
ukmt-pink-2017-03.body:
Antonia is the fifth to the left, so 4 girls are between them on that side; she is the eighth to the right, so 7 are between on the other side. Total $4+7+2=13$.

**Answer: (D) 13**

ukmt-pink-2017-04.title: Count turns
ukmt-pink-2017-04.body:
The circumference is $2\pi$, so rolling $11\pi$ turns the circle through $5\tfrac12$ turns. After 5 full turns it looks as at the start; a further half turn leaves it upside-down, which is picture D.

**Answer: (D)**

ukmt-pink-2017-07.title: Worst case
ukmt-pink-2017-07.body:
With 6 buttons the student may have exactly 2 of each colour. The 7th button must make three of one colour.

**Answer: (D) 7**

ukmt-pink-2017-15.title: Name the cells
ukmt-pink-2017-15.body:
Write the grid as $3,a,1\,/\,b,c,d\,/\,2,e,?$. The top-left block sum is $T=3+a+b+c$. Top-right: $a+1+c+d=T$ gives $d=b+2$. Bottom-left: $b+c+2+e=T$ gives $e=a+1$. Bottom-right: $c+d+e+\,?=T$ gives $c+b+2+a+1+\,?=a+b+c+3$, so $?=0$.

**Answer: (A) 0**

ukmt-pink-2017-18.title: Count negative products
ukmt-pink-2017-18.body:
The product is negative when one die is negative (3 of 6 faces) and the other positive (2 of 6 faces). Probability $2\times\frac36\times\frac26=\frac13$.

**Answer: (C) $\frac13$**

ukmt-pink-2017-25.title: Use midlines
ukmt-pink-2017-25.body:
Let $P$ be the midpoint of $GI$. In triangle $FGI$, $MP\parallel FI$ and $MP=\tfrac12FI$. In triangle $GHI$, $PN\parallel GH$ and $PN=\tfrac12GH$. Since $GH=FI$, $MP=PN$, so triangle $PMN$ is isosceles with $\angle PMN=\angle PNM=\angle NMH=\alpha$ (the last because $PN\parallel GH$). Because $MP\parallel FI$, $\angle IFH=\angle PMG=\angle PMN+\angle NMG=2\alpha$.

**Answer: (A) $2\alpha^\circ$**
